events.summary: Cabinet approved concessional loans of up to LKR 500,000 for public servants in 2026.
Cabinet capped fuel allowances for ministers, MPs and officials at March 1 fuel prices.
Cabinet approved a government subsidy of up to LKR 20 per litre for 92-octane petrol.
Cabinet approved six-month free tourist visas for passport holders from 39 countries.
The 2026 National Vesak event was designated for the historic Mithellawala Temple in Dihagoda.
Prime Minister said a Cabinet paper on Hill Country relief and infrastructure would be submitted soon.
Officials promised Ditwah-affected Hill Country residents homes and land worth at least LKR 5 million.
Authorities issued energy-saving instructions for government offices, streetlights and large events.
Parliamentary committee instructed officials to prepare an immediate plan for safe ash disposal.
Public Utilities Commission confirmed the second-quarter electricity tariff revision, effective April 1.
India delivered 38,000 metric tonnes of fuel to Sri Lanka during a supply crisis.
Supreme Court electronic case filing began.
Government launched a five-month national energy conservation programme.
A programme to provide hospitals with modern equipment is being implemented.
Health Ministry planned service and infrastructure improvements at the hospital.
Officials proposed GPS tracking for vehicles transporting minerals in the Northern Province.
Anti-corruption commission scheduled the digital asset declaration system launch.
Railway Department plans a digital ticketing pilot at six stations.
Police recruitment notice provides for 100 lawyers to join as assistant superintendents.
District Secretary suspended salt pan work pending review of land ownership.
Ceylon Petroleum Corporation plans QR registration for non-vehicle fuel users.
Committee decided to appoint five Petroleum Corporation officers for ministry fuel coordination.
Budget funds allocated for rehabilitation of Happagastenne estate hospital.
Rehabilitation work at Happagastenne estate hospital was underway.
Applications invited for appointing 453 medical graduates as primary medical officers.
Police announced additional traffic and security deployment for the New Year period.
Digital ticketing pilot planned for Kelani Valley railway line in April.
Court property clearance generated revenue from disposed case items in 2025.
March Aswesuma payments were credited to eligible seniors’ bank accounts.
Parliamentarian allocated 2026 decentralized funds to rehabilitate the tank’s first channel.
Cyclone-damaged road reconstruction work launched in Nuwara Eliya District.
Japan signed a grant agreement for disaster-response radio equipment.
Uva Provincial Council officials donated one day’s salary to the Rebuilding Sri Lanka Fund.
Minister and Swiss envoy discussed joint youth projects, focusing on vocational training.
Northern Province issued appointment letters to 51 public-service officers and drivers.
Cabinet approved schoolgirls' sanitary-pad vouchers worth 1,440 rupees per student.
Cabinet approved appointing a 12-member expert committee to prepare an energy-economy framework.
ADB agreed to raise this year's financing to $480 million.
Hospital opened the former presidential room for public patient treatment.
Authorities approved appointing a national education reform steering committee.
Renovation of Colombo Central Bus Station was completed ahead of April reopening.
Angoda mental health institute employees donated one day’s salaries to the Rebuilding Sri Lanka Fund.
Government committee reviewed progress on plans to establish a national nursing university.
Health officials directed hospitals to dispense two months of clinic medicines at once.
Postal deliveries will run on alternate days, with transport stopping each Wednesday.
The transport commission expects bus fares to rise by more than 10%; Cabinet approval is pending.
Colombo Municipal Council decided to resume parking fee collection from March 23.
Government kept schools open four days weekly, with Wednesdays off during the fuel shortage.
Ceylon Electricity Board proposed a 13% electricity tariff increase.
Government said it was spending Rs. 20 billion monthly on fuel subsidies.
Government launched data collection to assess fuel needs of food distribution vehicles.
Symphony Orchestra of Sri Lanka donated Rs. 1 million to the Rebuilding Sri Lanka Fund.
Plans call for Anti-Corruption Commission branch offices in all nine provinces.
Public health inspectors planned nationwide food safety inspections ahead of the festive season.
Funding allocated for 2,500 resettlement houses in the North and East.
Education Ministry to review procedures and coordinate school admissions for transferred doctors’ children.
Fuel cargo tenders were awarded for diesel, petrol, crude oil and aviation fuel.
Presidential Secretariat vehicle use fell from 833 vehicles to 634.
Lanka Sathosa offered discounts on 100 products and announced a customer prize draw.
Norway received a proposal to support renewable energy development and discussed possible projects.
The Petroleum Corporation decided to continue fuel distribution on Saturday and remain ready for Sunday supply.
Fuel distribution by vehicle number-plate digit resumed to reduce congestion at filling stations.
Government relaxed fuel access rules and enabled agricultural organisations to obtain fuel for farmers.
Second group of Sri Lankan local representatives completed governance training in India.
India-supported Bailey bridge opened on the Chilaw–Toduwawa road after Cyclone Ditwah.
First phase of Bambalapitiya Railway Station modernisation began.
Station modernisation is estimated to cost Rs. 60 million.
Fuel QR registration continues, with more than 5.5 million vehicles registered.
Authorities reviewed progress and plans under the national drug eradication campaign.
Colombo Municipal Council temporarily suspended vehicle parking fees in the city.
Teacher training and curriculum reviews continued under education reforms.
Cabinet approved four committees to recommend measures addressing global instability and its effects on Sri Lanka.
President instructed each ministry to submit a practical fuel conservation plan immediately.
Education Ministry set a four-day school week, making Wednesdays holidays until further notice.
Prime Minister said three committees had been appointed to manage the energy crisis.
Government reinstated QR fuel registration to manage fuel consumption amid global uncertainty.
Health Ministry staff in selected divisions may work from home each Wednesday to conserve fuel.
Three-year programme began to develop 322 community productivity model villages across Sri Lanka.
Consumer Affairs Authority plans nationwide festive-season inspections of goods sold above controlled prices.
Tourism Ministry decided to introduce a dedicated fuel QR system for registered tourism service providers.
Government is considering reintroducing work from home for public employees to conserve fuel.
Weekly passenger bus fuel allocations will increase from 60 to 360 litres based on distance travelled.
Authorities are updating fuel QR registration to address technical problems and vehicle ownership changes.
Police deployed nationwide to secure fuel stations and manage traffic queues.
Government decided to declare every Wednesday a public holiday to conserve energy.
Government declared Wednesdays public holidays to conserve energy amid fuel supply problems.
Public Administration Ministry temporarily cancelled government ceremonies and limited large gatherings.
Maskeliya public playground redevelopment began with federation funding for paths and facilities.
Government reintroduced QR fuel distribution ahead of possible holiday shortages.
Government considered a four-day work week and requested departmental recommendations.
Prime Minister proposed a 2027 preschool curriculum, teacher training, and regulatory oversight.
President directed officials to study working from home and submit a report.
President directed officials to correct and update the fuel QR system promptly.
Railway restoration is underway between Kandy and Badulla after landslide damage.
Minister committed to establish a new agricultural services centre, subject to district approval.
Recruitment event held for 2,918 nursing trainees selected for three-year training.
Updated draft of the National Media Policy was formally handed to the ministers.
Sabaragamuwa Province held an AI workshop for government executives.
India responded positively to Sri Lanka’s request for additional fuel stocks.
Mac Holdings donated Rs. 5 million to the Rebuilding Sri Lanka fund.
Health Ministry selected 2,918 nursing trainees and scheduled appointment letters.
Officials reviewed cyclone housing payment problems in affected districts.
Government expected two-stage payments for partially damaged homes without damage assessments.
Scholarship programme opened for top Advanced Level students to study at leading overseas universities.
Programme expects to invest Rs. 4,001 million in scholarships for 200 students through 2033.
Water Board plans supply from newly discovered groundwater to nearby communities facing shortages.
Ten accessible buses arrived in Hambantota for the Clean Sri Lanka pilot service.
Finger jetties at Wellamankara harbour were scheduled for implementation under the 2027 allocation.
C-Nor and the Fisheries Department were advancing repairs to Ditwah-damaged Chilaw harbour and fishing boats.
Government allocated about one billion rupees to expand student transport and add over 200 Sisu Sariya buses.
March Aswesuma benefits for first-stage beneficiaries were to be deposited into bank accounts.
March Aswesuma payments for second-stage beneficiaries were to be deposited into bank accounts.
Officials screened landless applicants to identify households for future legal land grants.
Economic monitoring committee met to discuss measures against external economic shocks.
Economic monitoring committee met to discuss measures against external economic shocks.
Fisheries Ministry began a six-month programme to restore cyclone-damaged fishing boats and equipment.
Repairs to partially damaged freshwater fishing boats were completed across nine districts.
Boat repairs continued at special camps in Gurunagar and Chilaw.
Foreign Employment Bureau allocated emergency funds to embassies assisting Sri Lankans in the Middle East.
Malabe Model Boys' College held its inaugural student parliament session under the Vision programme.
Cabinet approved free 14-day visa extensions for foreigners stranded by cancelled flights.
Cabinet approved raising relocation housing grants to LKR 2.5 million per household.
Four principal successor companies began operating under full state administration.
The Ceylon Electricity Board was dissolved and reorganized into four main and two subsidiary companies.
Cabinet restored pension entitlement for public officers who joined service after 2016.
The Transport Board issued appointment letters to 199 drivers and 342 conductors.
The budget allocated Rs. 2 billion to maintain service on unprofitable rural roads.
Government plans local advisory committees to identify suitable resettlement land in hill-country areas.
A two-day workshop for Open Parliament Initiative members concluded in Kalutara.
IOM and UNDP plan to launch LANTERN next month for land and trust-building in the North and East.
The Health Ministry began the fifth national oral health survey, covering all districts through November.
January 2026 Mahapola scholarship payments of Rs. 10,000 were deposited into eligible students’ accounts.
Court ordered first-phase excavation of the Kurukkalmadam mass grave to begin March 30.
Australian Federal Police opened a Colombo training workshop for Sri Lankan law enforcement agencies.
CEB dissolved and its functions transferred to six state-owned companies.
Officials were instructed to develop fuel supply arrangements prioritizing food production and fisheries.
Fisheries officials held drug prevention awareness sessions for fishers in four southern districts.
Navy personnel removed and disposed of waste at Karapitiya National Hospital.
Indian Navy vessel arrived in Colombo during a visit providing sailing training to Sri Lankan Navy personnel.
Ministry called applications for 2026/2027 vocational education courses for Grade 12 students.
Prime Minister said a salary committee would be appointed this year to address public-service pay disparities.
Sri Lanka arranged medical checks for the crew and transfer of the Iranian ship to Trincomalee.
Government allocated relief funds for Northern Province farmers affected by livestock losses.
Relief payments totaling Rs. 258.85 million were paid to affected farmers.
Free medicines worth Rs. 25 million were provided to treat surviving livestock.
A special Cabinet committee was formed to protect crops.
Foreign Ministry established a round-the-clock emergency response unit for Sri Lankans in the Middle East.
Japan and Kattankudy cooperative signed an agreement for school canteen reconstruction funding.
Cabinet approved allocations to rebuild cyclone-damaged schools and education colleges.
Initial cyclone relief payments of Rs. 25,000 were reported for affected people.
Government allocated funds for paddy purchases; procurement prices were increased.
Government set paddy purchase prices at LKR 120, 130 and 140 per kilogram by variety.
Budget allocated funds for journalists’ higher education scholarships and technical assistance.
Navy and Air Force began a joint rescue operation for crew of a stranded Iranian ship.
Police introduced a WhatsApp complaint number and established a ministry public complaints desk.
A provincial governor laid the foundation for a two-storey child care home.
Government extended stranded foreign visitors’ visas by two weeks without charge.
Funds were provided to all provinces to improve provincial school infrastructure.
Work is underway to modernise 50 vocational training centres with courses across 25 districts.
The government is preparing to introduce new Grade 6 education reforms from 2027.
The government approved a 14-day free visa extension for tourists stranded in Sri Lanka.
National drug prevention week began with awareness activities across government institutions and schools.
Lanka Coal Company invited tenders for emergency supply of 300,000 metric tons of coal.
Praja Shakthi held a training workshop for community development groups in Divulapitiya.
EU pledged additional humanitarian funding for communities affected by Cyclone Ditwah.
